reasoning_details.text:
The expected bundle output shows one "warning: " prefix on the first line, continuation lines without prefix. So the intended behavior is: only ONE prefix for the whole multi-line warning. This means the conversion must collapse the multi-line warning into a single LOG_WARNING() chain:

```cpp
LOG_WARNING()
    << "You are opting in to remove schema identifiers in the bundled schema.\n"
    << "The only legit use case of this advanced feature we know of is to workaround\n"
    << "non-compliant JSON Schema implementations such as Visual Studio Code.\n"
    << "Otherwise, this is not needed and may harm other use cases. For example,\n"
    << "you will be unable to reference the resulting schema from other schemas\n"
    << "using the --resolve/-r option.\n";
```

And "converted down to its LAST statement" means merge all statements into one, using the last statement's structure? Hmm. Actually re-reading once more: "A multi-line warning must be converted down to its LAST statement, not just its first — every continuation statement of the message goes through the helper too". 

Maybe the intended code style is each line as a separate `LOG_WARNING()` statement but... no, that gives multiple prefixes.

Hold on. Maybe LOG_WARNING is implemented such that it only prints the prefix conditionally based on stream state? No.

Let me reconsider: Maybe the intended conversion is a chain where the first line is a separate statement and continuations are chained onto it? Like:

```cpp
LOG_WARNING() << "line1\n"
              << "line2\n"
              ...
              << "lineN\n";
```

Then the whole thing is one statement. "converted down to its LAST statement" might be a garbled way of saying the statement now ends where the last std::cerr statement ended. The phrase "every continuation statement of the message goes through the helper too" = every continuation line is part of the helper chain.

Actually wait. There's another important clue: command_bundle.cc currently includes `<iostream> // std::cout`. After conversion, `std::cerr` no longer used there, so the include comment might change to `// std::cout`. Fine.

Now for resolver.h multi-line warning:
```cpp
std::cerr << "warning: No schema resources were imported from this file\n";
std::cerr << "  at " << entry.first.string() << "\n";
std::cerr << "Are you sure this schema sets any identifiers?\n";
```
Expected output presumably:
```
warning: No schema resources were imported from this file
  at /path
Are you sure this schema sets any identifiers?
```
Single prefix. Convert to a chain:
```cpp
LOG_WARNING()
    << "No schema resources were imported from this file\n"
    << "  at " << entry.first.string() << "\n"
    << "Are you sure this schema sets any identifiers?\n";
```

That's clearly the intended result. "converted down to its LAST statement" = collapse from the first statement down through the last into one chain.

Now, does the helper need to handle the prefix written once per call? Each warning site calls LOG_WARNING() once. Good. Even if multiple warnings of the same kind occur (e.g., multiple unknown rules), each gets its own "warning: " prefix — correct.

So implementing LOG_WARNING as:
```cpp
inline auto LOG_WARNING() -> std::ostream & {
  std::cerr << "warning: ";
  return std::cerr;
}
```

Now check any test expecting multi-line resolver warning. Let me search for "No schema resources were imported". It wasn't in the test grep output (only the phrase list showed bundle, lint, validate). So no test.

Now, behavioral change: JSONL empty and lint unknown rule warnings now always printed. Only non-verbose affected test: pass_jsonl_empty.sh. Update it to expect the warning.

Also need to check: does making lint unknown warning unconditional affect `fail_lint_only_unknown.sh`? Let me check that test — it uses `--only` unknown rule which is a different path ("Only enabling rule"?). Let me look. Actually `Only enabling rule: ...` is verbose. Unknown "only" rule may throw or print. Let me check tests quickly.

Actually simpler: after building, run full ctest and see failures. Let me now implement changes.

Let me also double check there aren't other "warning" occurrences not with colon, e.g. `std::cerr << "warning"`. Search for "warning" in src.
